items.q: What energy instruments can I trade?
items.a: Crude oil (Brent and WTI), natural gas and related energy products. The live quotes table above shows every energy instrument available on your account.

An energy CFD is a derivative that lets you gain exposure to price movements in energy commodities such as crude oil and natural gas without owning the physical asset. You can go long when you expect prices to rise or short when you expect them to fall, using leverage to manage your exposure.

items.q: What spreads are available on energy products?
items.a: Spreads on energy start from 0.03 pips and vary with market conditions. The live table on this page shows the current buy and sell prices.

items.q: What leverage is available for energy trading?
items.a: Maximum leverage on energy is up to 1:1000 at Tier 1 and reduces as position size increases. See the dynamic leverage page for the full schedule.

items.q: What are the trading hours for energy markets?
items.a: Energy markets trade Monday to Friday for about 23 hours a day, with a short daily break. Holiday hours can differ.
